title: tehas-plugin.json
description: A plugin's manifest, version 2: tehas-plugin.json at the root of the plugin's repository, at the pinned commit (operator spec 2.2, 2026-11-25-plugins-2.0.0-operator.md, revision 8.1, :402-437). The field table at :415-433 is the source; this schema is its draft until the console/xtask fixture task exists (spec :408-411), after which the table, the fixtures in api/fixtures/manifest/ and this schema are held to one verdict by the gate. Every object is closed: an unknown field is refused (spec :406), at every level, so a manifest made for a later tehas never runs half read. There is no license field yet: the licence is undecided and joins when it is decided (spec :435-437). skills are bare paths only (issue #3371, build-seat placement): a skill's about is its SKILL.md frontmatter description and its chats are that file's chats frontmatter, so the manifest carries neither; a manifest-level about or chats would sit outside the dist/ hash that parts 3 and 4 tie approval to (spec :445-520, :523 onward), which is a further reason the manifest stays paths-only until the roadmap manager decides #3371. The reader is console/core/src/plugin/manifest.rs; rules the reader holds that this schema leaves open are named in the field descriptions.

plugin.description: The spec's major (spec 2.2 table :415; the schema is named with "plugin": 2 at :405). Always present.

spec.description: The spec revision the plugin was built against, such as "2.0.0-r5", so its tags can state it (spec 2.2 table :416; example "2.0.0-r7" at :1323). 2.0.0-r8 is revision 8 with its errata). The pattern is exact and closed (#3381 forbids widening it): a dotted form such as 2.0.0-r8.1 is refused.

name.description: The plugin's name, a letter and up to 11 letters or digits — the contract's rule (spec 2.2 table :417). 5.1 (:856-858) relies on it being letters and digits only, since TEHAS_PLUGIN_ORIGINS_<NAME> upper-cases it. SPEC GAP: 'a letter' does not state case; lowercase is carried from the 1.x contract rule and the uppercase mapping at :856-858.

label.description: What people see (spec 2.2 table :418). The table says only 'text'; the manifest keeps 1.x's bound (kept: the menu, the confirm and the review line set it in 24) until the roadmap manager gives 2.0 its own, and this schema states it with the reader: one line of 1 to 24 characters, control characters refused.

kind.description: "plugin" or "adapter"; no; "plugin" (spec 2.2 table :419). Part 10 governs adapter (:1295-1370); an adapter has no driver entry, view, skill, hook, gate, tool or schedule (:1299), enforced below.

runtime.description: "starlingmonkey"; "component" for an adapter only (spec 2.2 table :420, parts 1 and 10.1). A manifest without runtime is the JavaScript path (:1320-1330); a component is one Rust component in dist/wasm/, named in the manifest, in place of a driver (:1267, 10.1 :1313-1318). The adapter-only rule is enforced by the allOf below.

timeout.description: Seconds, at most 600, for one run; needed with a driver (spec 2.2 table :421; 1.4's per-run time, :349). driver requires timeout and timeout requires driver (dependentSchemas) — the pairing follows from 'with a driver'. SPEC GAP: the table says 'seconds', not integer or number, and names no minimum; 1.x used integer 60..14400, which 2.0's 600 supersedes for the maximum only.

asks.description: Grant names, always present, may be empty (spec 2.2 table :422; part 5). The manifest only asks — nothing is granted from it alone (:841-848). An ask of http is refused to any plugin that is not an adapter (:1358), enforced by the allOf below. The table names no count; 32 is the reader's bound, kept (kept: a plugin asking more than a person can read in one review is refused, not waved through), and an ask named twice is refused. The closed vocabulary lives in part 5 and the host's own list, checked by the reader's grant module, not by this schema.

driver.description: The entry that exports run(ctx); needed with a driver, default dist/driver/main.js (spec 2.2 table :423; layout in the floating spec 2, :184-194 — 'its paths point into dist/'). SPEC GAP: the table says 'a path' with no grammar; this pins the dist/ prefix and forbids dot-segments, and the reader owns the rest (no absolute paths, no escape).

label.description: What a confirm names; a draft's confirm shows the exact title and body (spec 2.2 table :424; 6.3, floating spec :660-675, draws the confirm outside the frame naming this label). Required because a press of a person's action cannot confirm without it. It keeps the manifest label's bound: one line of 1 to 24 characters, control characters refused, since the confirm names it in the same space.

args.description: A JSON schema for the press's arguments (spec 2.2 table :424; 6.3: a press 'carries arguments under that action's schema', floating spec :633). Left open here: like 1.x's tool params, the reader (console/core/src/plugin/params.rs) keeps it to the closed part of JSON schema. SPEC GAP: the table lists {label, args} without saying whether args is needed; required here means the reader decides — see questions_for_tehas_d6.

actions.description: Id to {label, args}; no (spec 2.2 table :424). The presses a view may send (6.3). The ids keep 1.x's shape (a-z and -, 1 to 16, checked by the reader) and the count keeps 1.x's cap of 2 (kept: more presses than two is a menu, not a view). Ids are keys, so their emptiness is not constrained by this schema.

id.description: The view's id (spec 2.2 table :425), which names its /out folder and its ask view:<id>. It keeps 1.x's shape: a-z and -, 1 to 16.

entry.description: The view's entry in dist/view/ (spec 2.2 table :425; floating spec 2, :189). SPEC GAP: only 'its entry in dist/view/' is said; this pins the prefix and forbids dot-segments, the reader owns the rest.

views.description: Each view, its entry and its open; no (spec 2.2 table :425). All three keys are needed: the table's sentence reads id, entry and open as the view's whole shape. The count keeps 1.x's cap: 1 to 4 (kept: four is what the menu and the dock hold); an empty list names no view, so it is refused where an absent field is allowed.

skills.description: Skill files, paths under skills/; no (spec 2.2 table :426; floating spec 2 lists skills/ at the repository root, :192). Bare paths only: issue #3371 is open at the spec level, but the build seat has placed a skill's about in its SKILL.md frontmatter description and its chats in that file's chats frontmatter, so the manifest holds neither field. The count keeps 1.x's cap of 8 (kept: a chat's 8192-byte skill budget reads as eight at most). Each path is a folder of its own, skills/<id>/<file>, and is asked as skill:<id> with the folder's name; the .md ending and the per-path shape are the reader's.

at.description: The hook or gate point, as hook:<when>:<event> (spec 2.2 table :427; before-hooks carry an admin's policy at :599). SPEC GAP: the table gives the shape, not the <when> or <event> vocabularies; the reader checks the point exists.

entry.description: The hook's entry, a path into dist/ (spec 2.2 table :427; floating spec 2, :187). SPEC GAP: no grammar beyond 'a path' is given for hook entries; prefix pinned here, reader owns the rest.

hooks.description: Each hook or gate point; no (spec 2.2 table :427). SPEC GAP: no array cap is given; 1.x capped hooks at 1.

path.description: The module's file in dist/wasm/ (spec 1.1, :271; part 2's layout, floating spec :191).

source.description: The module's source in src/, for the rebuild layer (spec 1.1 audit layer 2, :322-326: 'The manifest may name a module's source in src/ and a recipe' — 'may', so not needed). A source names a folder, so its trailing slash is allowed here and nowhere else: path, driver, entry and component stay file-shaped and refuse a trailing slash.

recipe.description: The build recipe: a toolchain container pinned by digest, plus the build command (spec 1.1, :322-324). SPEC GAP: the table at :428 names the field; :322-324 names its contents but no JSON shape, so this schema leaves it open and the reader fixes it. Our own adapters must reach 'rebuilt from source: matches' (:1319-1321).

wasm.description: Name to {path, source, recipe}: the driver's modules; no (spec 2.2 table :428; part 1.1). path is needed, source and recipe are the audit's rebuild layer, which 1.1 says 'may' (:322). SPEC GAP: no name pattern or count cap is given; 1.1's size caps (8 MiB per module, 32 MiB per dist/wasm/, :352-353) are byte checks at vetting (part 3, :503), not manifest fields.

path.description: The module's file in dist/view/wasm/ (spec 6.1's layout, floating spec :510).

source.description: The module's source in src/, for the rebuild layer (spec 1.1, :322-326; the same audit applies to view modules, :275). Folder form, trailing slash allowed, as for wasm.source; path stays file-shaped.

recipe.description: The build recipe (spec 1.1, :322-324). SPEC GAP: shape open, as for wasm.

view_wasm.description: Name to {path, source, recipe}: the view's modules; no (spec 2.2 table :429; part 6.1). A vendored .wasm is listed here too (floating spec :517-521). SPEC GAP: same open items as wasm; 6.1's caps (dist/view/wasm/ 16 MiB, :354) are vetting checks, not manifest fields.

version.description: The library's version (spec 3, :483-486: 'The manifest names each with its version, its upstream source and a sha256 for each file'). No grammar is given; the reader takes one line of 1 to 32 characters, control characters refused, and vetting compares it against the upstream's own tag.

upstream.description: One of two exact forms and nothing else: npm:<name>@<version> (public registry, exact version) or git:<host>/<owner>/<repo>@<commit> (full commit, host named by the release — github.com today). A URL, a range, a tag or a branch is refused at vetting; the host builds the fetch URL from the form, never from manifest text (spec 3, :487-492). SPEC GAP: the host list is the release's (:489-490), so the pattern is general here and the reader checks the host against the release.

files.description: A sha256 for each file (spec 2.2 table :430; spec 3, :483-486). SPEC GAP: the table says 'each file's sha256' without a shape; this reads it as file-path to lowercase-hex-sha256 — the fixture task and the reader confirm. Whether keys are paths inside dist/vendor/<lib>/ is the reader's.

vendor.description: Library to {version, upstream, files}: verified libraries; no (spec 2.2 table :430; part 3, :483-503). They live in dist/vendor/<lib>/ and count toward their own larger cap (8 MiB, 1.4 :355), a vetting check, not a manifest field.

solid.description: The solid-js version the compiled JSX expects; needed with a compiled view (spec 2.2 table :431; part 6). SPEC GAP: no version grammar is given — exact version or range is open; the solid ⇒ views pairing below only says a solid needs views, because 'compiled view' is not visible to the schema and an uncompiled view must not be forced to carry one.

url.description: An exact origin: https, a lowercase A-label host, no port, no path, no wildcard (spec 5.1, :838-840; decision 68, :836: no pattern in 2.1; a glob in a manifest is refused, :841 and :904). SPEC GAP: vetting also refuses an IP literal, a trailing dot and user information (10.1, :1353-1355), which this pattern cannot all state; the reader refuses them too.

credential.description: Whether the origin takes the credential at all (spec 10.1, :1330-1337, :1351-1352). Widening never adds one (5.1, :835).

methods.description: The allowed methods (spec 5.1, :849-853: 'Each origin entry lists its allowed methods and its body'; a widened destination defaults to GET and HEAD, :852). minItems 1 follows from 'lists'. SPEC GAP: the method vocabulary and casing are not enumerated in the spec; the examples use GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE (:1331).

body.description: none or bounded(<bytes>) (spec 5.1, :849-852): the standard's §6 bounded, this host's extension carrying the byte count; a bare bounded takes 10.9's request-body cap of 8 MiB (:2507). SPEC GAP: no schema-side maximum is set on <bytes> — 10.9's caps are proposals the owners tune (:2496), so the request gate checks the number, not this schema.

origins.description: Id to {url, credential, methods, body}: declared destinations; no; any kind may declare it, as a request (spec 2.2 table :432; 5.1, 10.1). Granted only by the signed vetted entry or the person's approval by name (:843-848) — never from the manifest alone. SPEC GAP: no id pattern, count cap or emptiness rule is given.

world.description: The adapter world, such as "tehas:adapter@2.0.0" (spec 10.1, :1339; part 10.2). SPEC GAP: the interface-name form is read off the example; the spec states no grammar.

component.description: The one component, in dist/wasm/, named in the manifest, in place of a driver (spec 10.1, :1313-1315; example dist/wasm/adapter.wasm at :1340). Needed because the table's value column names it and an adapter's entry is the component; SPEC GAP: for a JavaScript adapter the field's meaning is open — the table says the adapter object is needed for an adapter, so the reader decides what component holds on that path.

realms.description: The realms the adapter serves (spec 2.2 table :433; example ["code-host", "tickets"] at :1341). SPEC GAP: realm vocabulary and item grammar are not given; minItems 1 is inferred from the table naming the field for an adapter that serves something.

ports.description: The ports the adapter maps (spec 2.2 table :433; example at :1342-1343; the port list itself is the contract's, 10.1 and routes.json at :1360-1368). The mapping lives in dist/routes.json under api/adapter-routes.schema.json, hashed with dist/, not in the manifest. SPEC GAP: port names are the registry's, not enumerated here; item grammar inferred from the examples.

credential.description: The kind of credential the adapter needs; the host maps the kind to what it has configured, and the manifest never holds a credential (spec 10.1, :1355-1358; example "github" at :1345). SPEC GAP: the kind vocabulary is the host's configuration (10.4), not enumerated in the spec.

adapter.description: {world, component, realms, ports, credential}: needed for an adapter only (spec 2.2 table :433; part 10). SPEC GAP: the table names the five keys as the object's shape; each key's needed-ness is read from the one full example at :1338-1346.

then.description: An adapter (spec 10.1): the adapter object is needed (:433), and an adapter has no driver entry, view, skill, hook, gate, tool or schedule (:1299) — driver, views, actions, skills, hooks, solid and view_wasm are refused. It may keep wasm (:1310-1317), origins and the http ask (:1358).

else.description: An ordinary plugin, kind "plugin" present or absent (the table's default at :419): the adapter object is refused (:433, 'an adapter only'); component is the adapter's runtime alone (:420, 10.1 :1313); and http is given to an adapter alone and refused to any other plugin (:1358).
